# WikipediaBiographiesProcess

**What it does.** One transaction per row of the input list. Goes through the PDD sections “Pesquisa do artigo” → “Extração dos dados”. Each row of the input list (CSV or XLSX with the columns `termo_de_busca`, `endereco_do_artigo`) becomes a transaction; the output `.xlsx` spreadsheet has the columns `URL`, `Nome completo`, `Nascimento`, `Morte`, `Nacionalidade`, `Ocupação` and is written only if ALL items succeed (all or nothing, by the nekkora_rpa `XlsxResultSink`). Optional in the PDD (the cell stays empty when the data is missing; nothing is invented): `Morte`.

Names in the code are in English. Page labels, list columns, spreadsheet headers, secret names and rejection codes
stay as they are: they are data and contracts (the mapping is in `manifest.json` → `naming`).

## How it is organized

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `automation/pages.py` | one class per screen: `SearchPage`, `ProfilePage` |
| `automation/process.py` | `WikipediaBiographiesProcess`: the order of the screens and the spreadsheet row |
| `automation/selectors.py` | `SelectorKey` (one key per element) and how each element is located |
| `main.py` | command line |
| `selectors.json` | the same targets, read by the nekkora_rpa runtime (generated from the same plan; never edit by hand) |
| `manifest.json` | revisions, hashes, `step_id` ↔ Studio step map, names and keys |

## Screens and what each method does

- **`SearchPage`** — Screen of the PDD section “Pesquisa do artigo”.
  - `search_article()` — Fills the field with ``search_term`` and submits with Enter.
- **`ProfilePage`** — Screen of the PDD section “Extração dos dados”: checks the page address and reads the profile data.
  - `check_page_address()` — Reads the page address and compares it with ``article_url``.
  - `read_profile_data()` — Reads the title, “Nome completo”, “Nascimento”, “Morte”, “Nacionalidade”, “Ocupação” and “Campo(s)”.

## How each element is located

| Key | Strategy | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| `SelectorKey.SEARCH_TERM_FIELD` | CSS `header input[name="search"]` | stable container + attribute |
| `SelectorKey.PROFILE_TITLE` | CSS `h1#firstHeading` | stable ID or test attribute |
| `SelectorKey.PROFILE_FULL_NAME` | XPATH `//tr[th[normalize-space(.)="Nome completo"]]//td` | row anchored by its heading (heading → cell, or term → definition) |
| `SelectorKey.PROFILE_BIRTH_DATE` | XPATH `//tr[th[normalize-space(.)="Nascimento"]]//td` | row anchored by its heading (heading → cell, or term → definition) |
| `SelectorKey.PROFILE_DEATH_DATE` | XPATH `//tr[th[normalize-space(.)="Morte"]]//td` | row anchored by its heading (heading → cell, or term → definition) |
| `SelectorKey.PROFILE_NATIONALITY` | XPATH `//tr[th[normalize-space(.)="Nacionalidade"]]//td` | row anchored by its heading (heading → cell, or term → definition) |
| `SelectorKey.PROFILE_OCCUPATION` | XPATH `//tr[th[normalize-space(.)="Ocupação"]]//td` | row anchored by its heading (heading → cell, or term → definition) |
| `SelectorKey.PROFILE_FIELDS` | XPATH `//tr[th[normalize-space(.)="Campo(s)"]]//td` | row anchored by its heading (heading → cell, or term → definition) |

nekkora_rpa acts only if the locator finds EXACTLY one element with the expected identity; none, or more than one, is an error (it never picks the first one).
